source_quote: Short-lifespan large and giant breed cohorts showed elevated dilated cardiomyopathy prevalence in cardiology registry data.
Short-lifespan heavy and large breeds had earlier-onset osteoarthritis prevalence in longitudinal screening programs.
Medium-lifespan breed populations demonstrated moderate hip dysplasia prevalence across multi-registry screening data.
Atopic dermatitis prevalence remained stable across medium-lifespan breed dermatology surveillance populations.
Long-lifespan toy and companion breed groups accumulated substantial periodontal disease burden with advancing age.
Long-lived small breed populations showed elevated patellar luxation prevalence across orthopedic screening cohorts.
Myxomatous mitral valve degeneration was highly prevalent in long-lived small companion breed lineages.
Otitis externa prevalence was moderate and consistent across medium-lifespan general practice canine populations.
Short-lifespan giant and deep-chested breeds carried significantly increased gastric dilatation-volvulus burden.
Long-lived geriatric cohorts showed cumulative chronic kidney disease prevalence in later-life veterinary surveillance.
